youtube.description: Your physical copy of Hollow Knight: Silksong hints at more free content than anyone expected, plus a giant expansion with no date beyond "coming soon." Here's what that means for your save and your wallet. Sources: GamesRadar+, Polygon and Eurogamer.

claims.claim: The Silksong physical edition manual says the world will expand with free content packs.
The manual calls Sea of Sorrow the first giant expansion.
Sea of Sorrow will be free for players.
The manual says Sea of Sorrow is coming soon.
Sea of Sorrow was announced with a 2026 release window.

issues.quote: hints at more free content than anyone expected
issues.problem: GamesRadar says there was 'little doubt' Team Cherry would add lots of content, and Eurogamer says it 'shouldn't be a huge shocker.' 'More than anyone expected' overstates the surprise. This is hype phrasing rather than a hard factual claim.

check.summary: The sources support the script's core claims. The physical manual promises free content packs, plural, and calls Sea of Sorrow the 'first giant expansion.' Polygon says the expansion will also be free. The manual gives only 'coming soon' despite the 2026 window. GamesRadar (reprinted on Steam News) says this reads like a step back from 2026, and players fear a 2027 delay. The 2027 delay is framed as a fear, not fact. The content packs come from official manual text, so not labelling the story as rumour is acceptable. The only issue is minor hype in the YouTube description.
